title: Heartbeat-gap triggered stale-drain tombstones and cascading fallback surge — investigation & corrective plan
creator: Ava Kline
description: Summary: On 2025-02-18 at ~03:12 UTC, our routing system experienced a sudden, sustained increase in fallback traffic to smaller model variants and cross-region failovers for customers in eu-west and us-central. The immediate symptom was a 4–6x spike in fallback volume and a concurrent P95 token latency increase for affected requests. Root cause analysis showed that a short (≈40s) gap in the node health heartbeats to the regional controller combined with a tombstone compactor edge-case allowed stale drain tombstones to persist. Routers saw persistent drain markers and redirected traffic away from healthy pools, cascading into overflow and automated variant fallbacks. This ticket captures the investigation timeline, decisions, and action items for remediation and prevention.
timeline: 2025-02-18 03:12 UTC — Alert: routing-fallback-rate > 400% on eu-west and us-central. 03:14 — On-call confirms increased fallback calls and variant swap logs. 03:18 — Observability shows cluster heartbeat aggregator missed 1 iteration for several nodes after a transient DB connection pressure. 03:25 — Regional controller created drain tombstones for ~12 host IDs; compactor job skipped in previous 10m window due to maintenance toggle. 03:40 — Routers continued to respect tombstones; autoscaler and tier-routing rules redistributed traffic causing capacity amplification in other regions. 04:05 — We rolled back the recent heartbeat aggregator change and re-enabled compactor; tombstones TTLs cleared and routing stabilized by 04:37. 04:45 — Post-incident team formed and initial notes posted to incident doc.
impact_details:
- Customers affected: ~120 tenants with requests routed through eu-west/us-central (estimated 0.9% of total traffic).
- Observed metrics: fallback volume +420% (15m), P95 token latency +78% on affected routes, 500-series errors up +1.2% for a 25-minute window.
- Business impact: several paid routes experienced degraded latency and increased cost due to cross-region egress and fallback model token usage.
root_cause: Two factors combined: (1) a transient DB connection pressure in the heartbeat aggregator caused ~40s of missed heartbeats for a subset of hosts; (2) the tombstone_compactor had been disabled by an earlier maintenance toggle and therefore did not expire tombstones when reconciliation would normally have removed them. The regional controller therefore left persistent drain tombstones attached to healthy hosts. Routers use tombstone presence as a hard preference to avoid hosts; because the tombstones were not cleared and our routing policy gives priority to avoiding drained hosts, traffic rebalancing triggered autoscaling and variant fallbacks in other regions, creating a feedback loop.
short_term_fixes_completed: Rolled back heartbeat aggregator change that increased DB connection pooling pressure (PR #8423) — reverted at 03:40 UTC.
Re-enabled tombstone_compactor and forced one compaction run to clear stale tombstones (PR #1295) — executed at 03:42 UTC.
Added temporary routing safety gate: routers now ignore drain tombstones older than 10 minutes while compactor lag is detected (hotfix) — deployed 03:50 UTC.
long_term_mitigations: Introduce explicit heartbeat TTL agreement: controller and router will share configured heartbeat_ttl; add validation to deployments to prevent TTL divergence (owner: Priya Raman, due: 2025-03-10).
Make tombstone compactor self-healing: if compactor misses >1 run, trigger immediate reconciliation and emit critical alert (owner: Marco Diaz, due: 2025-03-03).
Add circuit breaker on fallback rate: if fallback-rate > 200% for a route for >5m, temporarily throttle engine-level fallbacks and surface to human operator (owner: Sarah Li, due: 2025-03-15).
Improve DB client resilience in aggregator: reduce connection churn and add backpressure handling to avoid heartbeat misses during meta-db transient pressure (owner: Amit Kapoor, due: 2025-03-05).
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- We chose a short-term hotfix (ignore tombstones older than 10 minutes during compactor lag) to quickly restore traffic; tradeoff: small risk of briefly sending traffic to hosts that are purposely drained for maintenance. We mitigated by making the hotfix observational for 5 minutes before full enforcement.
- For long-term, we considered making routers tolerant to tombstones by probabilistic routing instead of a binary avoid rule. We rejected that for now since it complicates SLO guarantees; instead we'll add a circuit breaker to limit fallout when tombstones spike unexpectedly.
- We prioritized low-risk changes first (compactor toggles and rollback) to avoid cascading deployment risk during the incident window.

SRE: Add Grafana alert for tombstone-age > configured_threshold (Jamal Rivers) — Done — est 1 point.
Platform: Implement fallback-rate circuit breaker and dashboard (Sarah Li) — To Do — est 8 points.

learnings: Do not treat tombstone existence as a single source-of-truth without considering compactor health and compaction lag.
Small heartbeat gaps combined with disabled background housekeeping can create long-lived, high-impact routing state.
Having a short-term, automated safety gate (ignore-older-than) helped restore traffic quickly but must be guarded by monitoring to avoid unsafe restores during planned maintenance.
Observability gaps: add explicit tombstone-age and compactor-lag SLOs and alert thresholds.
next_steps: Complete the long-term mitigations across controller, router, compactor, and DB client by the due dates above. Follow-up retro with PMs and SRE to align release windows for the parts touching routing safety. Add a rehearse incident runbook for tombstone-compaction failure scenarios and include in on-call training.
